_comment: A standing 'pqp Live' dashboard: online users, voice (mesh vs livekit),
watch party and the infra basics, meant to be left up permanently (unlike
grafana-dashboard-event.json, which is scoped to one event window and
imported/removed per party). Standard Grafana dashboard JSON model:
Dashboards > New > Import, paste this file (or POST it to
/api/dashboards/db, see this directory's README).
Replace <PROMETHEUS_DATASOURCE_UID> and <LOKI_DATASOURCE_UID> with the
real UIDs from Administration > Data sources on import -- Grafana's own
import dialog also offers to remap them for you. On this stack today
those are the Grafana Cloud built-ins, uid `grafanacloud-prom` (Prometheus)
and `grafanacloud-logs` (Loki); same placeholder convention as
grafana-dashboard-event.json, not hardcoded here for the same reason that
file gives: nothing in this directory is provisioned from the repo, the
Grafana UI is the source of truth once imported, and this file is a
starting point, not a synced copy.
Every pqp_api_* panel needs tools/monitoring/pqp-api-metrics-exporter.py
installed and running on a box with a Prometheus textfile collector
(today: the self-hosted SFU box) -- without it those panels read 'No
data', which is the honest state, not a broken panel. As of this file's
authorship the exporter is NOT installed anywhere; see this directory's
README for the install command.
There is still no server-side count of concurrent HLS (watch party)
viewers anywhere in pqp -- same finding as grafana-dashboard-event.json's
'Watching' panel, carried over verbatim to the 'Watch party viewers' panel
below rather than inventing a number. The HLS panel that IS real graphs
sessions and rungs, which are transcode PROCESSES, not audience size.
'SFU box' (instance="sfu-pqp") and 'Egress box' (instance="sfu-hls") are
two different machines -- see the two-machine infra note in this
directory's README and CLAUDE.md's session-handover memory; do not merge
their panels, a saturated egress box says nothing about LiveKit and vice
versa.
Default range is 7 days with a 1 minute refresh, meant for a wall-mounted
or frequently-glanced-at view of product health, not an event war room
(that is grafana-dashboard-event.json's 3h/30s).
title: pqp Live

panels.title: Online users
panels.description: pqp has no field that dedupes by user, so this is open WebSocket sessions cluster-wide (one person in two tabs counts twice). See the pqp_api_users_online HELP text in pqp-api-metrics-exporter.py for the full reasoning. On one machine (today) the two series are equal.

panels.title: In voice calls
panels.description: mesh + livekit stack to the same total line drawn on top of them (voice.rooms[].participants summed by transport). mesh caps at MESH_VOICE_LIMIT (8) per room; a total that pulls away from mesh+livekit means a payload shape this exporter does not recognise, not a bug in the sum.

panels.title: Voice rooms by backend
panels.description: Count of voice.rooms[] by transport. Communities and servers of 10+ members are pinned to livekit; DM calls and smaller servers are pinned to mesh (server/src/voice/transport-policy.ts).

panels.title: Largest room now / peak today
panels.description: voice.largestRoomNow and voice.peakRoomSizeToday. The peak resets on deploy and at Sao Paulo midnight, so a sawtooth at midnight is expected, not a drop in usage.

panels.title: Watch party: sessions / rungs
panels.description: liveHls.sessions / liveHls.rungs: watch-party TRANSCODE processes, not audience size -- see the 'Watch party viewers' panel for why there is no viewer count next to it.

options.content:
**pqp does not count concurrent HLS viewers server-side.** The playlist proxy (`server/src/voice/hls-playlist-proxy.ts`) is a stateless, unauthenticated-per-request pull with no per-request access log, so there is no 'viewers' gauge to graph here without adding one (out of scope for a monitoring-only change; same finding as `grafana-dashboard-event.json`'s 'Watching' panel).

For a live party, read audience size off the stream itself (Twitch/YouTube viewer count). For a rehearsal, `tools/watch-party-load/src/hls-audience.ts`'s own progress output and final JSON summary are the closest thing pqp has to this number -- see `tools/watch-party-load/README.md`.

panels.title: SFU box CPU
panels.description: The LiveKit SFU box (tools/sfu-monitoring). Not the same machine as the egress/HLS box below -- see this panel's counterpart.

panels.title: Egress box CPU
panels.description: The watch-party transcode (HLS egress) box. This is the number that actually costs a party: rungHealth restarts and stalls correlate with this saturating.

panels.title: DB pool / breaker
panels.description: checks.pool from GET /ready plus runtime.db.breaker.state. A queue above zero is the earliest honest warning (docs/MONITORING.md); breaker open means every DB-dependent route is fast-failing with 503 (pitfall 17 in CLAUDE.md).

panels.title: API scrape health
panels.description: Every other panel on this dashboard depends on the exporter itself being alive. scrape_ok at 0, or seconds-since-last-scrape climbing past ~120 (the timer runs every 20s), means every pqp_api_* panel here is showing stale or absent data, not a quiet product.

panels.title: Screen share fps (presenter, by bucket)
panels.description: streamQuality.fpsBuckets.presenter, both transports summed: the PRESENTER's own encode rate, bucketed. A rising 5-9 line against a falling 30-plus line is the '5-6 fps' user report made visible on a graph instead of a ticket. See voice/stream-quality-metrics.ts.

panels.title: Screen share limitation reason (presenter)
panels.description: streamQuality.limitationReasons, both transports summed: WebRTC's own qualityLimitationReason on the presenter's encoder. reason=bandwidth climbing is the uplink talking (a starved upload); reason=cpu climbing is the machine/encoder talking -- the split this feature exists to make, so a choppy share gets the right fix instead of a guess.

panels.title: Screen share bitrate (presenter, by bucket)
panels.description: streamQuality.bitrateBuckets.presenter, both transports summed: read next to the fps panel -- low fps with a healthy bitrate bucket points at CPU/encoder (reason=cpu), low fps with a low bitrate bucket points at the uplink (reason=bandwidth).
